title: [Shortcut Guide] Crashes when opening the "PowerToys" tab

judgment.rationale: The repeated click-path failure and stack trace already identify a sharing violation while copying bundled shortcut manifests. The issue is on 0.100.2 and the reporter explicitly declined a diagnostic ZIP for privacy; current-version confirmation and privacy-conscious diagnostics are needed before deciding whether the lock still affects supported builds.
evidence: Clicking the Shortcut Guide PowerToys tab after opening with Win+Shift+> crashes every time on 0.100.2.
The provided IOException reports a locked +WindowsNT.Notepad.en-US.yml file during bundled-manifest copy, followed by a second-instance warning.
Automated triage already requested a bug report ZIP and latest-version confirmation; no reporter answer follows.

judgment.recommended_action: Ask whether the same crash occurs on the latest stable version and, if the reporter is comfortable sharing a reviewed diagnostic archive, request /bugreport immediately after repro; respect a refusal to share private data.

comment.body:
Thanks for the exact PowerToys-tab repro and the stack trace showing a sharing violation while Shortcut Guide copies `+WindowsNT.Notepad.en-US.yml`. I understand your concern about personal information in the diagnostic archive. To tell whether this is still a current-build issue and what holds the file, could you please provide:
1. The exact latest stable PowerToys version you test, and whether opening Shortcut Guide with Win+Shift+> then clicking the PowerToys tab still crashes on that version.
2. If you are comfortable sharing it, reproduce the crash and immediately submit a comment containing `/bugreport`; review the generated ZIP for sensitive information before uploading it. If you cannot share a ZIP, please say so rather than posting private data.
This distinguishes a resolved 0.100.2 failure from a current file-lock problem and lets us investigate the competing access safely.

status.label: Current-version confirmation needed
status.detail: The file-sharing failure is documented; no current-build confirmation or shareable fresh diagnostics follow the existing request.
